title: Ankhorage Runtime
summary: Renders Ankhorage application manifests and resolves their runtime bindings, capabilities, events, media, screens, and state.
purpose: Provide a platform-neutral runtime boundary that turns portable Ankhorage manifests into rendered application behavior without coupling consumers to a particular host application.
responsibilities: Render manifest-driven screens and component trees through configurable registries and renderer boundaries.
Resolve bindings, repeat data, state updates, media values, screen loaders, and component event actions.
Compose capability execution, runtime diagnostics, and authoring overlays through explicit runtime configuration.
boundaries: Does not define the portable manifest and descriptor contracts it consumes.
Does not provide product-specific screens, component implementations, or host application navigation.
Does not own provider-specific capability, data-source, storage, authentication, or deployment implementations.
audience: Application hosts that render Ankhorage manifests with React and React Native-compatible component registries.
Runtime and tooling maintainers integrating bindings, capabilities, state, media, or authoring behavior.
useCases: Render an application screen from a portable manifest and registered component implementations.
Execute a component event action and expose its operation lifecycle to the rendered UI.
Resolve stateful bindings, repeated content, media values, and screen operation loaders at runtime.

architecture.role: Platform-neutral manifest runtime with explicit React/React Native host and component registry boundaries.
invariants: Consumers provide host components and integrations through declared registries and configuration rather than sibling-source imports.
Portable contracts remain separate from executable runtime behavior.
Provider-specific behavior is composed through capability and data-source boundaries rather than embedded in the renderer.

limitations: Rendering requires React and compatible React Native or React Native Web peers supplied by the host.
The runtime can execute only capabilities, data sources, media resolvers, and components supplied through its public configuration boundaries.
